baselines: Trust-Hub-style structural checklist baseline: flags any flop within N hops of a scan_en-controlled mux without further discrimination (expected high false_positive_rate).
Empty/naive baseline (shipped default submission): trojan_detected=false with empty suspect lists, used to verify the evaluator fails naive non-answers.

metrics.description: Fraction of ground-truth suspect flops and muxes correctly identified in the submission (recall over the union of SR1/SR2 sets).
metrics.name: detection_rate

metrics.description: Fraction of submitted suspect_flops/suspect_muxes entries that are not present in the ground-truth sets (precision complement).
metrics.name: false_positive_rate

metrics.description: Whether the boolean trojan_detected field matches the ground-truth label (1.0 if correct, 0.0 otherwise).
metrics.name: trojan_label_accuracy

metrics.description: Wall-clock time in seconds taken by evaluate.py to grade the submission, including any optional iverilog/vvp cross-check simulation.
metrics.name: inference_latency

acceptance_criteria: A submission scoring PASS must list at least 3 of the 4 true key flops and at least 3 of the 4 true scan muxes, report trojan_detected=true, and provide a rationale referencing scan-mode/capture conditionality.
The shipped baseline (naive/empty) submission -- trojan_detected=false, empty suspect_flops/suspect_muxes, generic rationale -- must score FAIL under the grading rubric.
False positive rate must be computed as the fraction of submitted suspect_flops/suspect_muxes entries that do not appear in the ground-truth sets, and must be reported even on PASS submissions.

Optional simulation cross-check: if iverilog/vvp are available, evaluate.py may drive scan_en=1 and shift a known pattern through scan_in, then confirm key_ff0..key_ff3 values appear at scan_out at the expected shift-cycle offsets per scan_chain_order.txt, corroborating the ground truth independent of the submission.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: The netlist contains four key flip-flops key_ff0, key_ff1, key_ff2, key_ff3 holding a secret key register. In the reference (non-trojan) design these flops' scan_in path would be gated so scan capture never latches key state onto the scan chain (a scan-disable AND gate masks their D-input tap from the shift register during capture). In the trojan variant shipped here, four scan multiplexers u_smux_key0, u_smux_key1, u_smux_key2, u_smux_key3 are spliced directly between each key flop's functional D-input/Q-output and the adjacent scan-chain flip-flop's scan_in, selected by scan_en. This routes key_ff0..key_ff3 state into the shift register during scan capture, so it becomes observable at scan_out after the appropriate number of shift cycles once scan_en=1. Functional (scan_en=0) operation is bit-exact identical to a trojan-free version; the leak manifests only when scan_en is asserted and the chain is shifted.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Exact-match (case-insensitive) comparison of submitted suspect_flops set against the ground-truth key flop instance names extracted from the netlist; compute recall requiring all 4 be present.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly identify all four key flip-flop instances (key_ff0, key_ff1, key_ff2, key_ff3) as scan-observable in suspect_flops.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Exact-match comparison of submitted suspect_muxes set against ground-truth mux instance names; compute recall requiring all 4 be present and precision penalizing large numbers of unrelated extraneous instances.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly identify the four scan-splicing multiplexer instances (u_smux_key0..u_smux_key3) as the mechanism enabling the leak in suspect_muxes.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Direct boolean equality check against ground-truth label true.
security_requirements.requirement: trojan_detected must be reported as true, since the design under analysis is the trojan-inserted variant.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Keyword/semantic check for terms indicating scan-mode conditionality (e.g., 'scan_en', 'scan mode', 'capture', 'shift') combined with optional cross-check simulation via iverilog/vvp toggling scan_en to confirm key_ff values appear at scan_out, validating the reported mechanism actually reproduces the leak on the real netlist.
security_requirements.requirement: The rationale must demonstrate understanding that the leak is scan-mode-specific (i.e., manifests only when scan_en is asserted) rather than a general functional bug, distinguishing it from a naive false-positive flagging of unrelated flops.

hidden_spec.threat_model: Design-for-test (DFT) scan infrastructure is a standard manufacturing/test feature, but if secret-holding registers (e.g., a symmetric key register) are not explicitly isolated from the scan network, anyone with physical or remote scan access (test engineer, untrusted foundry, or an attacker with JTAG/scan port access post-deployment) can shift the key out through scan_out, defeating confidentiality guarantees that hold in normal functional mode. This converts a test feature into a full key-extraction channel.

constraints: Do not modify any file under inputs/; submit only submission/trojan_report.json.
The netlist inputs/key_core_netlist.v is provided as-is in structural Verilog (gate-level, using a small standard-cell-like library of DFF, MUX2, AND, OR, NOT primitives) and must not be edited.

Base your findings solely on static/behavioral analysis of the provided netlist and, optionally, simulation via yosys/iverilog/vvp against the provided scan_chain_order.txt; no other side-channel data is available.
expected_outputs: submission/trojan_report.json containing a trojan_detected boolean, a list of suspect flip-flop instance names, a list of suspect mux/gate instance names, and a free-text rationale

functional_requirements.requirement: trojan_report.json must be valid JSON parseable by a standard JSON library and must contain all five required top-level fields (trojan_detected, suspect_flops, suspect_muxes, confidence, rationale) with the exact types specified in the interface.

suspect_flops and suspect_muxes must each be JSON arrays of strings; every string listed must correspond to an actual instance name found in inputs/key_core_netlist.v (no fabricated or misspelled instance names).
confidence must be a numeric value in the inclusive range [0.0, 1.0].
rationale must be a non-empty string of at least 20 characters describing the reasoning used to identify the listed flops and muxes.

public_spec.interface: The submission is a single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json (UTF-8, no trailing comments). Required top-level schema: { "trojan_detected": <boolean>, "suspect_flops": [<string>, ...], "suspect_muxes": [<string>, ...], "confidence": <number 0.0-1.0>, "rationale": <string> }. "suspect_flops" must list exact Verilog instance names of flip-flop cells from inputs/key_core_netlist.v that the participant judges to be scan-observable in a way inconsistent with normal isolated operation. "suspect_muxes" must list exact instance names of the multiplexer/gating cells the participant judges responsible for splicing those flops onto the scan path. evaluate.py reads inputs/key_core_netlist.v (and optionally invokes iverilog/vvp to simulate scan_en/scan_in/scan_out behavior against inputs/scan_chain_order.txt) purely for reference and cross-checking; it does not execute or modify the submission file. Field names, casing, and types above are exact and mandatory; unrecognized extra fields are ignored.
public_spec.objective: Analyze the supplied gate-level netlist of a small crypto core with an embedded scan-test infrastructure. The design integrates a scan chain (ports scan_en, scan_in, scan_out) alongside a functional key register. Your task is to review the netlist and produce a structured analysis report identifying which flip-flops are reachable on the scan-out path during scan-mode capture-and-shift, and which specific mux instances establish that reachability, so that test engineers can assess whether test infrastructure inadvertently exposes internal state that should remain functionally isolated from the scan network.
public_spec.response_format: JSON or Markdown report plus generated artifacts as requested.

title: Scan-capture path leaking a key register
